key_insight: UnDA transfers useful structure across unpaired medical image modalities by aligning semantically meaningful class tokens and down-weighting uncertain predictions.
clinical_relevance: It could help improve segmentation performance when paired scans are unavailable, which is common in real clinical data collection.
method: Attention-based Alignment Module extracts class tokens in a backbone-agnostic way
Uncertainty-Weighted Optimal Transport (UCT-OT) suppresses noisy supervision during feature alignment
Per-class ProtoNCE keeps stable prototypes to preserve class-level separability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains on representative segmentation tasks under strictly unpaired settings, including better accuracy and boundary precision in the target modality.
watch_item: Performance may depend on prediction confidence quality and careful tuning of alignment and prototype-memory components across heterogeneous datasets.
paper_title: UnDA: Unpaired Domain Alignment for Cross-Modal Knowledge Transfer in Medical Imaging
